tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). ## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Firecrawl
Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts. Firecrawl provides web, developer, government, and research search, and executes catalogued Alexandria data providers. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes; authenticated searches also return matching Alexandria providers in data.tools. firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and provider contracts; firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_scrape with a url retrieves one supplied page. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and code documentation and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a legal or regulatory question, firecrawl_gov_search searches primary law and regulatory material from US federal, state, and local government sources: statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications; firecrawl_search with categories: ["gov"] reaches the same sources in the web group and cannot be combined with other categories. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. Search and discovery tools are read-only and return ranked results. firecrawl_search_feedback records a quality rating for a prior firecrawl_search by its id. Billing: web, developer, and research search are billed per request; government search is free; Alexandria discovery (firecrawl_search with sources ["alexandria"] alone, and firecrawl_find_tools) is free; firecrawl_scrape is billed, as a page retrieval in url mode or at each executed capability's listed price in alexandria mode.

## claude.ai Google Docs

---
name: gws-cli-default
description: "Google (Drive, Sheets, Gmail, etc.) work goes through the gws CLI by default; no raw API/OAuth token handling"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 16900c66-2198-452d-ac4b-bcbcdb631977
  modified: 2026-11-02T18:24:11.971Z
---

Use the `gws` CLI (`/opt/homebrew/bin/gws`) as the default way to interact with Google services. Do not export its credentials or call Google APIs directly with tokens.

**Why:** Eric said so on 2026-10-22 ("use gws-cli as the default way to interact with google") after I tried to speed up Drive wave 2 by exporting the gws OAuth login and calling the Drive API over HTTPS; the auto-mode classifier also denied that.

**How to apply:** Script Google work as `gws <service> <resource> <method>` subprocess calls, parsing stdout only (stderr carries a keyring line). Each call takes about 2.5 s, and more threads do not help (4 and 12 threads both gave ~70 files/min on 10-22), so plan long jobs as overnight runs. Traps (2026-10-29): a download (`files get` with `"alt":"media"` and `-o <file>`) must land inside gws's working directory, or it fails with "outside the current directory": run gws with `cwd=` the target folder and a bare file name. Uploading new content to an existing file is `files update --upload <path> --upload-content-type <mime>`; compare the returned `md5Checksum` with the local `md5 -q`. Content search is `"q": "fullText contains '...'"` (~2 s, PDFs included); `drive_index.py find --inside` wraps it. **Never run gws without the login keychain** (`env -i`, a stripped env, a sandbox): gws 0.22 cannot unlock `~/.config/gws/credentials.enc`, deletes it, and every later call fails "No credentials" until Eric runs `gws auth login` in a browser (2026-11-02: one `env -i` test broke the backup's Drive receipt). A launchd job is fine; test a job's PATH with `env -i … /usr/bin/env node -v`, never a gws call. Related: [[drive-fuse-read-hang]], [[gws-forms-api]].
---
name: cloud-push-launchd-blocked
description: "cloud-push under launchd: macOS per-file com.apple.macl blocks it; fixed 2026-10-23 by running it inside Terminal via cloud-push-launch.sh"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 802ea68a-c53e-4d3a-a897-1d311560fdd1
  modified: 2026-10-23T12:24:59.589Z
---

`com.keystone.clouddrivepush` (07:00 and 17:30) failed under launchd from 2026-10-12 to 10-23 with rsync `open: Operation not permitted` on `Drive/.../_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV/`. By hand from Terminal it always worked.

**Cause (tested 2026-10-23).** A process started straight by launchd (python3 or bash) can stat, mkdir and create new files in the Drive mount, and rewrite files it made itself. It cannot list Drive folders, or open, rename over, or delete files that Terminal made. Each such file carries `com.apple.macl` naming Terminal; `xattr -d` does not remove it. Full Disk Access on `Python.app`/rsync does not help (tried 10-14). rsync lists the destination, so it failed on the first step.

**Fix (live 2026-10-23).** The plist runs `/bin/bash ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push-launch.sh`. That runs `open -g -a Terminal ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.command`, which runs `cloud-push.py` (rsync, unchanged) with Terminal's access. The launcher waits 90 s for a new `START` line in `cloud-push.log`; if none, it writes an ERROR to the log and to `.errors.log`. Tracked plist copy: `~/.claude/scripts/com.keystone.clouddrivepush.plist`. Proven: kickstarted runs OK 07:15 and 07:21 with the screen locked.

**Known costs.** Each run opens a Terminal window. Eric set profile "Clear Dark" to "Close if the shell exited cleanly" (10-23, in Terminal Settings; a `defaults import` did not reach the running Terminal), so the window closes when the copy ends (tested). Under memory pressure Terminal ran queued opens ~5 min late; the 90 s check would log that as an ERROR even if the copy runs later.

**How to apply:** Do not swap rsync for a launchd-run copier: Terminal-made files can never be updated that way, and a by-hand run re-taints files. By hand is still `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py`, or `launchctl kickstart gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Off switch: `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Any other launchd job that must read or change Terminal-made Drive files hits the same wall; route it through Terminal the same way or use the `gws` API. See [[automation-cadence]] and [[cloud-copy-approval]].
---
name: pwsh-launchd-wrapper-trap
description: "Swapping pwsh from powershell/tap to Homebrew core breaks every launchd .ps1 job: core's bin/pwsh is a bash wrapper launchd refuses (tested, rolled back 2026-10-24)"
metadata:
  type: project
---

The deprecated powershell/tap pwsh 7.5.2 is a real Mach-O binary; Homebrew core's powershell installs bin/pwsh as a bash wrapper (DOTNET_ROOT=... exec libexec/pwsh). launchd cannot start that wrapper as ProgramArguments[0] on this macOS. Related: [[automation-cadence]], [[cloud-push-launchd-blocked]].

**Why:** On 2026-10-24 brew install homebrew/core/powershell (7.6.8) made /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh a #!/bin/bash wrapper; launchd killed com.keystone.morning and agysync with OS_REASON_CODESIGNING (Launch Constraint Violation, failure proc /bin/bash). Rolled back to the tap's 7.5.2 real binary within 5 minutes; jobs re-ran OK.

**How to apply:** Before the swap (tap disabled 2027-06-18; stack-check fails from 2027-03-01): prepend /bin/bash to ProgramArguments in every plist that starts /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh (KeystoneOS/ops/com.keystone.*.plist; a test agent with /bin/bash /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh ran OK), reload each, kickstart each, and test daily-backup-login.sh (it execs caffeinate ... pwsh). Core needs no admin password. Its dotnet dependency is ~700 MB.
---
name: long-jobs-in-terminal
description: "Jobs over ~30 min run in Eric's terminal (Ghostty since 2026-11-02) under caffeinate, not inside Claude Code; never auto-restart one after a kill"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Long jobs (about 30 minutes or more) run in Eric's own terminal, Ghostty (2026-11-02), under caffeinate, not as Claude Code background tasks. If one is killed, do not restart it on your own; resume only when Eric asks.

**Why:** Claude Code kills long background jobs under memory pressure and cannot reap them: the 10-26 Drive trash run died at ~7,500 of 30,968 files (session b1b9233e). Eric set the rule 2026-10-27.

**How to apply:** Hand Eric one command to paste in Ghostty, wrapped in 'caffeinate -i -s' (-s holds only on AC power). Make it resumable (skips done work). After a kill, report where it stopped and resume only when Eric asks. Example: ~/DEV/drive-tools/docs/STATUS.md (trash_twins.py).
---
name: text-eric-imessage
description: "Text Eric via iMessage (~/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh); standing rule since 2026-11-01: text him whenever a long run finishes or fails"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 2d5c93b0-f48c-48ce-a2fc-59cc2f50d48a
  modified: 2026-11-03T18:19:53.632Z
---

Claude can text Eric's iPhone with ~/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh "message". It sends an iMessage through the Mac's Messages app; the phone number is stored in the macOS Keychain (item text-eric-number). Set up and tested 2026-10-31. The script signs every text with a leading "From Claude: " (Eric asked 2026-10-31 so he knows it is from Claude); do not add a second signature.

**Why:** Eric asked 2026-10-31 for a way for Claude to text him; Messages on the Mac sends iMessage, no new accounts. On 2026-11-01, after asking for a text on three long runs in a row, he made it standing: "when ever you finish a long run on something you text me when your complete".

**How to apply:** Run ~/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh "<one line>" (Mac only; number in Keychain item text-eric-number, never write it to a synced file). **Standing rule (Eric, 2026-11-01): text him unasked whenever a long run finishes** (a job of about 30+ minutes, or any background or launchd job he is waiting on), and also when one fails. Send it after the result is verified and saved (not when the job merely exits), one line, lead with what to act on or "no action needed". Other texts only when he asks. See [[long-jobs-in-terminal]]. Exit 0 means Messages accepted it, not proof of delivery.

**If it fails with "AppleEvent timed out (-1712)"** (2026-11-03, Messages open 3+ h, no dialog on screen): restart Messages yourself (`osascript -e 'tell application "Messages" to quit'`, then `open -a Messages`), then resend. That fixed it. Do not ask Eric to look for a pop-up. Separate quirk, harmless: on macOS 27.2, asking some accounts for `service type` one by one gives -10000; the script's `whose` lookup still works.
#!/bin/bash
# Text Eric's phone through the Mac's Messages app (iMessage). Mac only.
# Usage: ~/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh "message"
# The number lives in the macOS Keychain (item text-eric-number), never in a synced file.
set -euo pipefail
msg="${1:?usage: text-eric.sh \"message\"}"
# Every text is signed at the start (Eric 2026-10-31), where the lock screen preview shows it.
case "$msg" in "From Claude:"*) ;; *) msg="From Claude: $msg" ;; esac
num="$(security find-generic-password -s text-eric-number -w)"
osascript - "$num" "$msg" <<'OSA'
on run argv
  tell application "Messages"
    set svc to 1st account whose service type = iMessage
    send (item 2 of argv) to participant (item 1 of argv) of svc
  end tell
end run
OSA
echo "sent"

**How to apply:** Do not swap rsync for a launchd-run copier: Terminal-made files can never be updated that way, and a by-hand run re-taints files. By hand is still `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py`, or `launchctl kickstart gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Off switch: `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Any other launchd job that must read or change Terminal-made Drive files hits the same wall; route it through Terminal the same way or use the `gws` API. See [[automation-cadence]] and [[cloud-copy-approval]].
---
name: pwsh-launchd-wrapper-trap
description: "Swapping pwsh from powershell/tap to Homebrew core breaks every launchd .ps1 job: core's bin/pwsh is a bash wrapper launchd refuses (tested, rolled back 2026-10-24)"
metadata:
  type: project
---

The deprecated powershell/tap pwsh 7.5.2 is a real Mach-O binary; Homebrew core's powershell installs bin/pwsh as a bash wrapper (DOTNET_ROOT=... exec libexec/pwsh). launchd cannot start that wrapper as ProgramArguments[0] on this macOS. Related: [[automation-cadence]], [[cloud-push-launchd-blocked]].

**Why:** On 2026-10-24 brew install homebrew/core/powershell (7.6.8) made /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh a #!/bin/bash wrapper; launchd killed com.keystone.morning and agysync with OS_REASON_CODESIGNING (Launch Constraint Violation, failure proc /bin/bash). Rolled back to the tap's 7.5.2 real binary within 5 minutes; jobs re-ran OK.

**How to apply:** Before the swap (tap disabled 2027-06-18; stack-check fails from 2027-03-01): prepend /bin/bash to ProgramArguments in every plist that starts /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh (KeystoneOS/ops/com.keystone.*.plist; a test agent with /bin/bash /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh ran OK), reload each, kickstart each, and test daily-backup-login.sh (it execs caffeinate ... pwsh). Core needs no admin password. Its dotnet dependency is ~700 MB.
---
name: long-jobs-in-terminal
description: "Jobs over ~30 min run in Eric's terminal (Ghostty since 2026-11-02) under caffeinate, not inside Claude Code; never auto-restart one after a kill"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Long jobs (about 30 minutes or more) run in Eric's own terminal, Ghostty (2026-11-02), under caffeinate, not as Claude Code background tasks. If one is killed, do not restart it on your own; resume only when Eric asks.

**Why:** Claude Code kills long background jobs under memory pressure and cannot reap them: the 10-26 Drive trash run died at ~7,500 of 30,968 files (session b1b9233e). Eric set the rule 2026-10-27.

**How to apply:** Hand Eric one command to paste in Ghostty, wrapped in 'caffeinate -i -s' (-s holds only on AC power). Make it resumable (skips done work). After a kill, report where it stopped and resume only when Eric asks. Example: ~/DEV/drive-tools/docs/STATUS.md (trash_twins.py).
---
name: text-eric-imessage
description: "Text Eric via iMessage (~/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh); standing rule since 2026-11-01: text him whenever a long run finishes or fails"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 2d5c93b0-f48c-48ce-a2fc-59cc2f50d48a
  modified: 2026-11-03T18:19:53.632Z
---

Claude can text Eric's iPhone with ~/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh "message". It sends an iMessage through the Mac's Messages app; the phone number is stored in the macOS Keychain (item text-eric-number). Set up and tested 2026-10-31. The script signs every text with a leading "From Claude: " (Eric asked 2026-10-31 so he knows it is from Claude); do not add a second signature.

**Why:** Eric asked 2026-10-31 for a way for Claude to text him; Messages on the Mac sends iMessage, no new accounts. On 2026-11-01, after asking for a text on three long runs in a row, he made it standing: "when ever you finish a long run on something you text me when your complete".

**How to apply:** Run ~/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh "<one line>" (Mac only; number in Keychain item text-eric-number, never write it to a synced file). **Standing rule (Eric, 2026-11-01): text him unasked whenever a long run finishes** (a job of about 30+ minutes, or any background or launchd job he is waiting on), and also when one fails. Send it after the result is verified and saved (not when the job merely exits), one line, lead with what to act on or "no action needed". Other texts only when he asks. See [[long-jobs-in-terminal]]. Exit 0 means Messages accepted it, not proof of delivery.

**If it fails with "AppleEvent timed out (-1712)"** (2026-11-03, Messages open 3+ h, no dialog on screen): restart Messages yourself (`osascript -e 'tell application "Messages" to quit'`, then `open -a Messages`), then resend. That fixed it. Do not ask Eric to look for a pop-up. Separate quirk, harmless: on macOS 27.2, asking some accounts for `service type` one by one gives -10000; the script's `whose` lookup still works.
#!/bin/bash
# Text Eric's phone through the Mac's Messages app (iMessage). Mac only.
# Usage: ~/.claude/scripts/text-eric.sh "message"
# The number lives in the macOS Keychain (item text-eric-number), never in a synced file.
set -euo pipefail
msg="${1:?usage: text-eric.sh \"message\"}"
# Every text is signed at the start (Eric 2026-10-31), where the lock screen preview shows it.
case "$msg" in "From Claude:"*) ;; *) msg="From Claude: $msg" ;; esac
num="$(security find-generic-password -s text-eric-number -w)"
osascript - "$num" "$msg" <<'OSA'
on run argv
  tell application "Messages"
    set svc to 1st account whose service type = iMessage
    send (item 2 of argv) to participant (item 1 of argv) of svc
  end tell
end run
OSA
echo "sent"

"""Build the two ARC docs for Eric's 11/05 hour block with Kenny Boyd (Kenny look).

ARC (Athletics Research Council) replaces BAIR (Eric, 2026-10-29). Kenny gave ARC to Eric
at the 2026-10-28 Tech Sync and asked for questions, about 3 people to involve, and the
research-request workflow "visible again as a checklist". The checklist is condensed from
01_Process (approval form, expedited review quick reference) and the Jan 2026 framework
(docs/program/framework-current-jan2026.md: weights and score bands come from there only).

Outputs:
    04_Committee/ARC_OnePage_KENNY_ER_<DATE>.docx (+ .pdf)
    01_Process/ARC_Research_Request_Checklist_KENNY_ER_<DATE>.docx (+ .pdf)
Run:  uv run --no-project --with python-docx python scripts/build_arc_docs.py
"""
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DEV = ROOT.parent
# shortcut: KennyDoc and word_pdf are imported from their home repos, not copied; if ARC
# gets its own repo, vendor kenny_doc.py + templates/kenny_template.docx into it.
sys.path.insert(0, str(DEV / "NCAA_BestPractices_Doc" / "scripts"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(DEV / "Tech_Inventory_Analysis" / "scripts"))
from kenny_doc import KennyDoc   # noqa: E402
from doc_platform import word_pdf  # noqa: E402

DATE = "2026-10-29"
FOR = [["For", "Kenny Boyd"],
       ["Prepared by", "Eric Rash, Applied Performance"],
       ["Discussion", "Thursday, November 5, 2026"]]
BOX = "☐ "   # empty check box


def one_page():
    d = KennyDoc("Athletics Research Council (ARC)",
                 deck="One front door between Baylor Athletics and campus research. "
                      "ARC replaces BAIR and widens its scope.",
                 status="Draft for discussion")
    d.meta(FOR)
    d.section("What ARC does", numbered=False)
    d.table(["Part", "What it is", "Where it stands"], [
        ["Research in", "Researchers ask to study our athletes or use our data. "
                        "ARC scores the request and decides.",
         "Built under BAIR. One-page checklist attached."],
        ["ARC sessions", "Campus researchers show how their work helps Athletics now. "
                         "20 min talk, 10 min discussion, recorded.",
         "New. Proposed first speaker: Michael Scullin, sleep and team travel."],
        ["Front door to campus", "Partnerships across all of Baylor, not only athlete performance.",
         "Goal for the May meeting with academic leadership."],
    ], widths=[1.4, 3.1, 2.0])
    d.section("What carries over from BAIR", numbered=False)
    d.para("ARC replaces BAIR and keeps its three pillars (Human Performance, Character "
           "Formation, Business Enterprise), its review process and forms, and the proposals "
           "already in review.")
    d.section("Path to May", numbered=False)
    d.table(["When", "What"], [
        ["Thu Nov 5", "Agree on this plan, the questions below and the people to involve."],
        ["Thu Nov 19", "Draft to you: ARC session plan and the renamed process materials."],
        ["Fri Dec 4", "Materials to Dr. Sarah Schnitker for review before anything goes public."],
        ["Fri Dec 11", "Your approval; date set for the council's first meeting."],
        ["Spring (proposed)", "First ARC sessions, internal."],
        ["May", "Soft launch at the meeting with academic leadership."],
    ], widths=[1.4, 5.1])
    d.section("Questions for you", numbered=False)
    d.numbered([
        "Members: carry over the BAIR members, or start a new group?",
        "Authority: does ARC approve research, or recommend to you?",
        "Scope: all research with Athletics, or performance and health first?",
        "Date: when does the council meet first?",
        "Name: what do we call the research and innovation lane that ARC sits in?",
    ])
    d.section("Three people to involve (no outreach until you agree)", numbered=False)
    # From Drive 04_RESEARCH/Faculty_Research_Partners_2026-10 (the "Start here" rows).
    d.table(["Name", "Role", "Why this person"], [
        ["Brian Garner", "Assoc. Prof., Mechanical Eng.", "Joint loading models; force plate checks."],
        ["Scott Koziol", "Assoc. Prof., Electrical & Computer Eng.", "Contactless readiness and fatigue checks."],
        ["Yang Li", "Professor, Electrical & Computer Eng.", "Wearables built into athlete apparel."],
    ], widths=[1.1, 2.6, 2.8])
    return d


def checklist():
    d = KennyDoc("ARC Research Request Checklist",
                 deck="How a research request moves from proposal to decision. "
                      "The steps are BAIR's; the name is new.",
                 status="Draft for discussion")
    d.meta(FOR)
    d.table(["1. Proposal", "2. Interest", "3. Review", "4. Approval"], [
        ["Researcher sends the ARC form", "Fit and feasibility: pass or fail",
         "Route the request, then score it", "Decide, write it down, file it"],
        ["Researcher", "ARC coordinator", "Subgroup of 3 or full council [Kenny: confirm]",
         "ARC council [Kenny: confirm]"],
    ], widths=[1.6, 1.6, 1.7, 1.6])

    def boxes(items):
        for t in items:
            d.para(BOX + t, space_after=1)

    d.section("1. Proposal: the form has four parts", numbered=False)
    boxes(["**Aim:** background, research question, method, timeline.",
           "**Fit:** how it serves the Baylor and Athletics mission, and which department.",
           "**Data:** NIH data guidelines; data stays Baylor's; confidentiality; monitoring plan.",
           "**Money and people:** funding, budget, staff pay, equipment and space, oversight."])
    d.section("2. Interest: any \"no\" sends it back with feedback", numbered=False)
    boxes(["Expertise in house, or a partner who has it.",
           "Equipment, technology, data and staff are available.",
           "Timeline fits the academic calendar and the sports seasons.",
           "IRB, NCAA and data privacy steps are manageable."])
    d.section("3. Review: full council if any answer is yes", numbered=False)
    d.para("Minors or other protected groups? A change to practice or competition? New athlete "
           "testing over 15 minutes? Staff time over 4 hours, or several departments? Outside "
           "partners or media? Sensitive topics? A new policy question? 3 or more sports?",
           space_after=2)
    d.para("**All no:** a subgroup of 3 decides within 1 week and tells the council. "
           "**Unsure:** full council.")
    d.section("4. Approval: score, decide, file", numbered=False)
    d.table(["Score area", "Points", "Total score", "Decision"], [
        ["Strategic alignment", "30", "75-100", "Approve, with resources"],
        ["Athlete and staff burden", "25", "50-74", "Approve if capacity allows"],
        ["Revenue and resources", "20", "25-49", "Revise and resubmit"],
        ["Research quality", "15", "0-24", "Decline"],
        ["Gender equity", "10", "", ""],
    ], widths=[2.1, 0.8, 1.1, 2.5], numeric_cols=(1,))
    boxes(["Decision letter to the researcher.",
           "IRB approval and budget confirmed before any data collection.",
           "Filed as Under review, Approved, or Declined or deferred (never deleted); results to the council."])
    return d


# Word (sandboxed on the Mac) stalls on a hidden "grant access" dialog when it saves into this
# repo, and macOS blocks this process from reading Word's own container. Word does save into
# ~/.cache/word-pdf (tested 2026-11-03; /var/folders temp dirs fail), so export there, then move.
SCRATCH = Path.home() / ".cache" / "word-pdf"


def export_pdf(docx, pdf):
    """Word's page count when `pdf` was written now, else None (with the reason printed)."""
    SCRATCH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp_pdf = SCRATCH / Path(pdf).name
    tmp_pdf.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    pages = word_pdf(str(docx), str(tmp_pdf))
    if pages is None or not tmp_pdf.exists():
        print(f"[error] Word did not export {Path(pdf).name}")
        return None
    try:
        shutil.copy2(tmp_pdf, pdf)
    except OSError as e:
        Path(pdf).unlink(missing_ok=True)   # no half-written PDF left behind
        print(f"[error] PDF copy failed, nothing left at {pdf}: {e}")
        return None

        ["Researcher", "ARC coordinator", "Subgroup of 3 or full council [Kenny: confirm]",
         "ARC council [Kenny: confirm]"],
    ], widths=[1.6, 1.6, 1.7, 1.6])

    def boxes(items):
        for t in items:
            d.para(BOX + t, space_after=1)

    d.section("1. Proposal: the form has four parts", numbered=False)
    boxes(["**Aim:** background, research question, method, timeline.",
           "**Fit:** how it serves the Baylor and Athletics mission, and which department.",
           "**Data:** NIH data guidelines; data stays Baylor's; confidentiality; monitoring plan.",
           "**Money and people:** funding, budget, staff pay, equipment and space, oversight."])
    d.section("2. Interest: any \"no\" sends it back with feedback", numbered=False)
    boxes(["Expertise in house, or a partner who has it.",

           "Timeline fits the academic calendar and the sports seasons.",
           "IRB, NCAA and data privacy steps are manageable."])
    d.section("3. Review: full council if any answer is yes", numbered=False)
    d.para("Minors or other protected groups? A change to practice or competition? New athlete "
           "testing over 15 minutes? Staff time over 4 hours, or several departments? Outside "
           "partners or media? Sensitive topics? A new policy question? 3 or more sports?",

    d.para("**All no:** a subgroup of 3 decides within 1 week and tells the council. "
           "**Unsure:** full council.")
    d.section("4. Approval: score, decide, file", numbered=False)
    d.table(["Score area", "Points", "Total score", "Decision"], [
        ["Strategic alignment", "30", "75-100", "Approve, with resources"],
        ["Athlete and staff burden", "25", "50-74", "Approve if capacity allows"],
        ["Revenue and resources", "20", "25-49", "Revise and resubmit"],
        ["Research quality", "15", "0-24", "Decline"],
        ["Gender equity", "10", "", ""],
    ], widths=[2.1, 0.8, 1.1, 2.5], numeric_cols=(1,))
    boxes(["Decision letter to the researcher.",
           "IRB approval and budget confirmed before any data collection.",
           "Filed as Under review, Approved, or Declined or deferred (never deleted); results to the council."])
    return d


# Word (sandboxed on the Mac) stalls on a hidden "grant access" dialog when it saves into this
# repo, and macOS blocks this process from reading Word's own container. Word does save into
# ~/.cache/word-pdf (tested 2026-11-03; /var/folders temp dirs fail), so export there, then move.
SCRATCH = Path.home() / ".cache" / "word-pdf"


def export_pdf(docx, pdf):
    """Word's page count when `pdf` was written now, else None (with the reason printed)."""
    SCRATCH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp_pdf = SCRATCH / Path(pdf).name
    tmp_pdf.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    pages = word_pdf(str(docx), str(tmp_pdf))
    if pages is None or not tmp_pdf.exists():
        print(f"[error] Word did not export {Path(pdf).name}")
        return None
    try:
        shutil.copy2(tmp_pdf, pdf)
    except OSError as e:
        Path(pdf).unlink(missing_ok=True)   # no half-written PDF left behind
        print(f"[error] PDF copy failed, nothing left at {pdf}: {e}")
        return None

"""What the two document builders need from the machine they run on.

Both Eric's machines build these documents: the MacBook (~/DEV) and the Baylor
Windows laptop (~/Desktop/DEV). Everything platform-specific lives here so the
builders stay about the document.

  add_doc_style_to_path()  finds ~/DEV/Program/Baylor_Doc_Style on either machine
  export_date()            the date stamp of the newest raw/ export
  word_pdf()               PDF + page count from Word itself
  chrome_path()            headless Chrome, for the exec summary's HTML twin
"""

import datetime
import glob
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def add_doc_style_to_path():
    # Not a sibling of ROOT: inside a .claude/worktrees/ checkout there is none.
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    for c in (os.environ.get("BAYLOR_DOC_STYLE"),
              os.path.join(home, "DEV", "Program", "Baylor_Doc_Style"),
              os.path.join(home, "Desktop", "DEV", "Program", "Baylor_Doc_Style"),
              os.path.join(home, "DEV", "Baylor_Doc_Style"),
              os.path.join(home, "Desktop", "DEV", "Baylor_Doc_Style")):
        if c and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(c, "baylor_docstyle.py")):
            sys.path.insert(0, c)
            return c
    sys.exit("[error] Baylor_Doc_Style not found. Set BAYLOR_DOC_STYLE to its folder.")


def export_date():
    """Date of the newest raw export - the same file clean_inventory.py reads."""
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "raw", "Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx")))
    if not files:
        sys.exit("[error] no raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx found")
    m = re.search(r"(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", os.path.basename(files[-1]))
    return datetime.date.fromisoformat(m.group(1))


def long_date(d):
    """September 15, 2026 - the style the 2026-09-01 documents settled on."""
    return "{} {}, {}".format(d.strftime("%B"), d.day, d.year)

"""Temporary watcher for the 11/05 print packet (Decision Desk 2026-11-03-drive-edit-watch, A).

Every 30 min (launchd, scripts/com.erash11.arcpacketwatch.plist) it asks Drive whether any
of the 5 packet sources changed. Eric edits them on Drive from the Mac and Windows, so the
Drive copies are the edit copies (docs/STATUS.md). On a change it downloads all 5, rebuilds
the packet the way a936542 did (agenda v2, ARC one-pager, checklist, Beyond Engineering
page 2, email page 1), saves it under a new name in 04_Committee (never overwrite), replaces
the content of the Drive packet PDF (same id, so links keep working), and texts Eric. No
change: nothing happens. Any failure: one text (repeats of the same error stay quiet).
After Thu 2026-11-05 12:00 Central it removes its own launchd agent.

Drive is reached only through the gws CLI. Word exports the .docx files
(build_arc_docs.export_pdf, via ~/.cache/word-pdf).

Run:   ~/.local/bin/uv run --no-project --with python-docx python scripts/watch_packet_1105.py [--seed | --dry-run]
  --seed     record the current Drive state as "already built" (install step)
  --dry-run  rebuild from Drive into ~/.cache/arc-watch/runs/ only: no repo copy, no Drive
             upload, no state change, no text (it checks Messages answers instead).
             The file ~/.cache/arc-watch/dry-run does the same for one launchd run.
"""
import datetime as dt
import fcntl
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
HOME = Path.home()
WATCH = HOME / ".cache" / "arc-watch"
STATE = WATCH / "state.json"
DRY_FLAG = WATCH / "dry-run"
LABEL = "com.erash11.arcpacketwatch"
PLIST = HOME / "Library" / "LaunchAgents" / f"{LABEL}.plist"
DEADLINE = dt.datetime(2026, 11, 5, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/Chicago"))
TEXT = HOME / ".claude" / "scripts" / "text-eric.sh"
GWS = "/opt/homebrew/bin/gws"
DOCX = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document"

# Packet order = page order. pages: which pages of the export go in (None = all).
SOURCES = [
    {"key": "agenda", "label": "agenda v2", "id": "14sRstASG76b13LPGTKgGo2ZMZ_3ns2I-", "kind": "docx", "pages": None},
    {"key": "onepager", "label": "ARC one-pager", "id": "1LMdImJEhxscTdy9_QwLgT6VqpLtXjd5E", "kind": "docx", "pages": None},
    {"key": "checklist", "label": "checklist", "id": "1qYPzgr-GI9B1BWQZ5NDXYdsUxBEDT7M_", "kind": "docx", "pages": None},
    # shortcut: the page picks assume the 11-03 exports (2 pages each: sheet page 1 is the
    # full-width tab, email page 2 is internal notes). Another page count -> all pages + a note.
    {"key": "faculty", "label": "Beyond Engineering sheet", "id": "1-AwqklBsFyqc23DHbvtVZGMyiECCR6AmAXvgwW7l_jg", "kind": "export", "pages": (2, 2)},
    {"key": "email", "label": "outreach email", "id": "1P-7on2DZu6vQR4T93mAn_uhVM2NxAB1u0OexUsywsS4", "kind": "export", "pages": (1, 2)},
]
PACKET_ID = "1UFbFYICduUNcQTuTK8hElJnm4cyl84QO"      # Drive 04_RESEARCH/04_Committee
PACKET_FOLDER = "1AjL6WZpz5puQse2J0NCt2qiVEoIStShJ"
PACKET_NAME = "ARC_Packet_2026-11-05_KENNY_ER_2026-11-03.pdf"
FIELDS = "modifiedTime,headRevisionId,md5Checksum,version,trashed,name"


def log(msg):
    print(f"{dt.datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} {msg}", flush=True)


def gws(args, cwd=None, timeout=180):
    """Run gws; return parsed stdout JSON. stderr carries a keyring line, so only stdout is read."""
    r = subprocess.run([GWS, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd, timeout=timeout)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gws {' '.join(args[:3])} exit {r.returncode}: {(r.stdout or r.stderr).strip()[:200]}")
    return json.loads(r.stdout) if r.stdout.strip() else {}


def meta(file_id):
    return gws(["drive", "files", "get", "--params", json.dumps({"fileId": file_id, "fields": FIELDS})])


def fingerprint(m):
    # Google-native files have no headRevisionId/md5Checksum; version covers them.
    return {k: m.get(k) for k in ("modifiedTime", "headRevisionId", "md5Checksum", "version")}


def load_state():
    return json.loads(STATE.read_text()) if STATE.exists() else None


def save_state(s):
    tmp = STATE.with_suffix(".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(s, indent=1))
    tmp.replace(STATE)


def text(msg):
    """One line to Eric. On the Messages -1712 timeout: restart Messages and retry once."""
    for attempt in (1, 2):
        r = subprocess.run(["/bin/bash", str(TEXT), msg], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        if r.returncode == 0:
            log(f"texted: {msg}")
            return True
        log(f"text failed (try {attempt}): {(r.stderr or r.stdout).strip()[:200]}")
        if attempt == 1 and "-1712" in (r.stderr + r.stdout):
            subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", 'tell application "Messages" to quit'], timeout=60)
            time.sleep(3)
            subprocess.run(["open", "-g", "-a", "Messages"], timeout=60)
            time.sleep(10)
        else:
            return False
    return False


def pages(pdf):
    out = subprocess.run(["pdfinfo", str(pdf)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return int(next(l.split()[-1] for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith("Pages:")))


def ensure_word():
    # word_pdf's own note: Word blocks on an invisible dialog if it is not already open.
    if subprocess.run(["pgrep", "-x", "Microsoft Word"], capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
        subprocess.run(["open", "-g", "-a", "Microsoft Word"], check=True)
        time.sleep(20)


def build_packet(run):
    """Download the 5 sources into `run`, return (packet path, notes)."""
    from build_arc_docs import export_pdf   # needs python-docx (uv --with python-docx)
    parts, notes = [], []
    for s in SOURCES:
        if s["kind"] == "docx":
            name = f"{s['key']}.docx"
            gws(["drive", "files", "get", "--params", json.dumps({"fileId": s["id"], "alt": "media"}),
                 "--output", name], cwd=run)
            src = run / name
            if not src.exists() or src.stat().st_size == 0:
                raise RuntimeError(f"{s['label']}: download empty")
            ensure_word()
            pdf = run / f"{s['key']}.pdf"
            if export_pdf(str(src), str(pdf)) is None:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Word could not export the {s['label']}")
        else:
            pdf = run / f"{s['key']}_full.pdf"
            gws(["drive", "files", "export", "--params", json.dumps({"fileId": s["id"], "mimeType": "application/pdf"}),
                 "--output", pdf.name], cwd=run)
            if not pdf.exists() or pdf.stat().st_size == 0:
                raise RuntimeError(f"{s['label']}: export empty")
            page, expect = s["pages"]
            n = pages(pdf)
            if n == expect:
                one = run / f"{s['key']}.pdf"
                subprocess.run(["pdfseparate", "-f", str(page), "-l", str(page), str(pdf), str(one)], check=True)
                pdf = one
            else:
                notes.append(f"{s['label']} now {n} pages, all included")
        parts.append(pdf)
    packet = run / PACKET_NAME
    subprocess.run(["pdfunite", *map(str, parts), str(packet)], check=True)
    return packet, notes


def upload(packet, state):
    """Replace the Drive packet's content (same id, links keep working); create one if it is gone."""
    file_id = state.get("packet_id", PACKET_ID)
    try:
        gone = meta(file_id).get("trashed", False)
    except RuntimeError:
        gone = True
    if gone:   # never delete or untrash on Drive: make a new file beside it
        r = gws(["drive", "files", "create", "--json", json.dumps({"name": PACKET_NAME, "parents": [PACKET_FOLDER]}),
                 "--upload", packet.name, "--upload-content-type", "application/pdf",
                 "--params", json.dumps({"fields": "id,md5Checksum"})], cwd=packet.parent)
    else:
        r = gws(["drive", "files", "update", "--params", json.dumps({"fileId": file_id, "fields": "id,md5Checksum"}),
                 "--upload", packet.name, "--upload-content-type", "application/pdf"], cwd=packet.parent)
    local = subprocess.run(["md5", "-q", str(packet)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
    if r.get("md5Checksum") != local:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Drive md5 {r.get('md5Checksum')} != local {local}")
    state["packet_id"] = r["id"]
    return r["id"]


def turn_off():
    log("deadline passed: removing the launchd agent")
    PLIST.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    # Last step: bootout ends this process too.
    subprocess.run(["launchctl", "bootout", f"gui/{os.getuid()}/{LABEL}"])


def main():
    args = set(sys.argv[1:])
    WATCH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lock = open(WATCH / "lock", "w")
    try:
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
    except BlockingIOError:
        log("another run holds the lock; skipping")
        return 0
    if dt.datetime.now(DEADLINE.tzinfo) >= DEADLINE:
        turn_off()
        return 0
    dry = "--dry-run" in args or DRY_FLAG.exists()
    DRY_FLAG.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    state = load_state()

    if "--seed" in args:
        if state:
            log("state already seeded; delete state.json first to reseed")
            return 1
        save_state({"files": {s["key"]: fingerprint(meta(s["id"])) for s in SOURCES}, "last_error": None})
        log("seeded current Drive state")
        return 0
    if state is None and not dry:
        log("no state.json: run --seed first")
        return 1

    try:
        now = {s["key"]: fingerprint(meta(s["id"])) for s in SOURCES}
        changed = [s["label"] for s in SOURCES if state is None or now[s["key"]] != state["files"].get(s["key"])]
        if not changed and not dry:
            log("no change")
            if state.get("last_error"):
                state["last_error"] = None
                save_state(state)
            return 0
        log(f"{'dry run' if dry else 'changed'}: {', '.join(changed) or 'none'}")
        run = WATCH / "runs" / dt.datetime.now().strftime("%m%d-%H%M%S")
        run.mkdir(parents=True)
        packet, notes = build_packet(run)
        n = pages(packet)
        if dry:
            r = subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", 'tell application "Messages" to count of accounts'],
                               capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
            log(f"dry run built {packet} ({n} pages); Messages check: rc {r.returncode} {(r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()[:120]}")
            return 0
        stamp = dt.datetime.now().strftime("%m%d-%H%M")
        out = ROOT / "04_Committee" / PACKET_NAME.replace(".pdf", f"_r{stamp}.pdf")
        if out.exists():
            raise RuntimeError(f"{out.name} already exists")
        shutil.copy2(packet, out)
        upload(packet, state)
        state["files"] = now          # the state read BEFORE download: a later edit still shows as a change
        state["last_error"] = None
        save_state(state)
        extra = f" ({'; '.join(notes)})" if notes else ""
        text(f"ARC packet rebuilt, {n} pages: {', '.join(changed)} changed{extra}. "
             f"Drive copy updated; Mac copy 04_Committee/{out.name}. No action needed.")
        return 0
    except Exception as e:   # noqa: BLE001 - any failure gets one text, then a retry next run
        err = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:160]
        log(f"FAILED {err}")
        if not dry and state is not None and state.get("last_error") != err:
            state["last_error"] = err
            save_state(state)
            text(f"ARC packet watch failed, Drive packet not updated: {err}")
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# B.A.I.R. Steering Committee

Baylor Athletics Innovation & Research. Research governance for the department:
the proposal review framework, the evaluation criteria, and the active study pipeline.

## Repo layout

Mirrors the `04_RESEARCH` structure on the primary storage drive:

- `01_Process/` — the review process itself, criteria, templates, workflow docs
- `02_Proposals/` — submissions, organized as Under_Review / Approved / Declined_or_Deferred
- `04_Committee/` — committee membership, meeting materials, minutes, decisions

Not copied here (they live on the drive and are either large, in flux, or outside
governance scope): `03_Active_Studies`, `05_Reporting`, `06_Grants`, `07_Admin_Tools`,
`_INBOX`, `_Archive`, `_Mark_for_Deletion`.

Source: `04_RESEARCH` on the primary storage drive.

## Conventions

- New studies land in `04_RESEARCH\_INBOX` on the drive first, then get filed
- Proposals move between the three `02_Proposals` subfolders as decisions are made;
  a proposal is never deleted, only moved to Declined_or_Deferred
- Committee decisions get written down in `04_Committee`, not left in email

## Related

- S2_Evaluation, ForcePlate_DecisionSystem, RTP_WorkingGroup (studies in the pipeline)
- Education_Alignment_Initiative (shares the B.A.I.R. umbrella)

    """Replace the Drive packet's content (same id, links keep working); create one if it is gone."""
    file_id = state.get("packet_id", PACKET_ID)
    try:
        gone = meta(file_id).get("trashed", False)
    except RuntimeError:
        gone = True
    if gone:   # never delete or untrash on Drive: make a new file beside it
        r = gws(["drive", "files", "create", "--json", json.dumps({"name": PACKET_NAME, "parents": [PACKET_FOLDER]}),
                 "--upload", packet.name, "--upload-content-type", "application/pdf",
                 "--params", json.dumps({"fields": "id,md5Checksum"})], cwd=packet.parent)
    else:
        r = gws(["drive", "files", "update", "--params", json.dumps({"fileId": file_id, "fields": "id,md5Checksum"}),
                 "--upload", packet.name, "--upload-content-type", "application/pdf"], cwd=packet.parent)
    local = subprocess.run(["md5", "-q", str(packet)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
    if r.get("md5Checksum") != local:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Drive md5 {r.get('md5Checksum')} != local {local}")
    state["packet_id"] = r["id"]
    return r["id"]


def turn_off():
    log("deadline passed: removing the launchd agent")
    PLIST.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    subprocess.run(["launchctl", "bootout", f"gui/{os.getuid()}/{LABEL}"])


def main():
    args = set(sys.argv[1:])
    WATCH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lock = open(WATCH / "lock", "w")
    try:
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
    except BlockingIOError:
        log("another run holds the lock; skipping")
        return 0
    if dt.datetime.now(DEADLINE.tzinfo) >= DEADLINE:
        turn_off()
        return 0
    dry = "--dry-run" in args or DRY_FLAG.exists()
    DRY_FLAG.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    state = load_state()

    if "--seed" in args:
        if state:
            log("state already seeded; delete state.json first to reseed")
            return 1
        save_state({"files": {s["key"]: fingerprint(meta(s["id"])) for s in SOURCES}, "last_error": None})
        log("seeded current Drive state")
        return 0
    if state is None and not dry:
        log("no state.json: run --seed first")
        return 1

    try:
        now = {s["key"]: fingerprint(meta(s["id"])) for s in SOURCES}
        changed = [s["label"] for s in SOURCES if state is None or now[s["key"]] != state["files"].get(s["key"])]
        if not changed and not dry:
            log("no change")
            if state.get("last_error"):
                state["last_error"] = None
                save_state(state)
            return 0
        log(f"{'dry run' if dry else 'changed'}: {', '.join(changed) or 'none'}")
        run = WATCH / "runs" / dt.datetime.now().strftime("%m%d-%H%M%S")
        run.mkdir(parents=True)
        packet, notes = build_packet(run)
        n = pages(packet)
        if dry:
            r = subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", 'tell application "Messages" to count of accounts'],
                               capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
            log(f"dry run built {packet} ({n} pages); Messages check: rc {r.returncode} {(r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()[:120]}")
            return 0
        stamp = dt.datetime.now().strftime("%m%d-%H%M")
        out = ROOT / "04_Committee" / PACKET_NAME.replace(".pdf", f"_r{stamp}.pdf")
        if out.exists():
            raise RuntimeError(f"{out.name} already exists")
        shutil.copy2(packet, out)
        upload(packet, state)
        state["files"] = now          # the state read BEFORE download: a later edit still shows as a change
        state["last_error"] = None
        save_state(state)
        extra = f" ({'; '.join(notes)})" if notes else ""
        text(f"ARC packet rebuilt, {n} pages: {', '.join(changed)} changed{extra}. "
             f"Drive copy updated; Mac copy 04_Committee/{out.name}. No action needed.")
        return 0
    except Exception as e:   # noqa: BLE001 - any failure gets one text, then a retry next run
        err = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:160]
        log(f"FAILED {err}")
        if not dry and state is not None and state.get("last_error") != err:
            state["last_error"] = err
            save_state(state)
            text(f"ARC packet watch failed, Drive packet not updated: {err}")
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
